findings.evidence: Never write "human error" as a root cause: it ends the analysis where it should start.
findings.fix: Models already know this rule from blameless-postmortem practice, but they may not apply it unprompted. Merge it into the line-30 item as one sentence ("Never name a person or 'human error' as the cause: write the action and the condition that made it reasonable, because blame stops reporting and ends the analysis"). This keeps both reasons and drops nothing.

findings.evidence: No eval covers the rule 'When a metric and a log disagree, show both, take the log time for the event and the metric time for impact' (SKILL.md line 26). The conflicting-times eval only tests two exports of the same chat.
findings.fix: Add an eval with a deploy log and a metrics CSV that disagree by a few minutes. Assert that the output shows both times, uses the log time for the event row and the metric time for impact, and marks the claim reported.

findings.evidence: 7. **Self-check before output:** every row has a UTC time, a source and a status; ... every reported claim is in the unverified list.
findings.fix: Close the loop: "If any check fails, fix the row, figure or list it names and run the whole check again; output only when every check passes."

findings.evidence: Step 3: "confirmed" (two independent sources, or a log line). Line 26: when a metric and a log disagree ... mark the claim "reported" until a third source settles it.
findings.fix: Add an exception to step 3 so the two rules agree: "... or a log line, unless a metric contradicts it (see Conflicting timestamps)."
